title: Should we break up? A quiz with no score, just 10 honest questions
summary: A should we break up quiz that won't hand you a score. Ten honest questions, and what your answers say about the conversation you need next.
body_markdown:
If you searched for a "should we break up" quiz, you probably want someone to just tell you. Ten questions, add up the points, get an answer.


We can't do that, and neither can any other quiz. A score doesn't know your relationship. It doesn't know if this has been a bad month or a bad three years. Two people can give the same ten answers and need to do opposite things.


So this one has no points and no result. It is ten questions to answer honestly, on your own. Write the answers down if you can, because it is harder to dodge a question on paper. At the end you won't get a verdict. You'll have a better idea of which conversation you need to have next.


## How things are day to day


**1. When something good happens, are they still the first person you want to tell?** Not who you tell first out of habit. Who you want to tell.


**2. When was your last good week together?** Not a good day or a nice dinner. A whole week where being together felt easy. If you have to think hard, notice that.


**3. Are you yourself around them, or a more careful version?** Think about what you stop yourself from saying, and how often.


## The problem itself


**4. What is the main problem, in one sentence?** "We fight a lot" doesn't count. Try for the thing under the fights. If you can't write the sentence yet, that is the first thing to work out, before any decision.


**5. Have you said that sentence to them, plainly, when you were both calm?** Yelling it in a fight doesn't count. Hinting doesn't count either.


**6. When you bring it up, what do they do?** Do they listen, get defensive, agree and then change nothing, or change for two weeks? Go by what actually happened the last few times, not what you hope would happen.


**7. If this problem never changed, could you live with it?** Not if it got a bit better. If it stayed exactly like this for the next ten years.


## Your side of it


**8. If money, housing and other people's opinions were all taken care of, what would you do?** This one separates[being scared to leave](https://www.ourmaia.com/post/i-want-to-leave-but-im-scared) from wanting to stay. They feel alike and they are not the same thing.


**9. Are you still trying?** Be honest. Some people asking this question stopped trying a while ago and haven't admitted it. Others are[the only one still trying](https://www.ourmaia.com/post/im-the-only-one-trying-in-my-relationship) .


**10. Picture a year from now. You're still together and nothing is different. What is your first reaction?** The first one, before you start arguing with it.


## The question people skip


In Maia conversations, people who are thinking about breaking up can usually answer questions 8 and 10 in a few seconds. They already know what they'd do if it were easy. The one they get stuck on is question 5. They have had the same fight many times, but when we ask if they've ever said the plain sentence to their partner on a calm day, the answer is often no. Their partner knows there is a problem. They may not know it is this serious.


That matters, because you can't really know how question 7 turns out until question 5 has happened.


## No score. Here is what your answers are for


Look at where you got stuck. It points to one of three places.


**You couldn't answer 4, 8 or 10.** You don't know yet what the problem is or what you want. The next conversation is with yourself, not your partner. Bringing it to them now usually turns into another fight about nothing in particular.


**You could answer those, but 5 was a no, or 6 was "I don't actually know."** The next conversation is with your partner. One calm talk where you say the sentence from question 4 and then watch what they do with it over the next few weeks. A break is sometimes a way of avoiding this talk, so read[how breaks tend to go](https://www.ourmaia.com/post/is-taking-a-break-the-fast-track-to-breaking-up) before you suggest one.


**You have said it plainly, more than once, and nothing changed. And your answer to 7 was no.** You may already have your answer, and what you're looking for is permission. No quiz can give you that. If you're still going back and forth, this piece on[breaking up or keeping trying](https://www.ourmaia.com/post/should-i-break-up-or-keep-trying) goes further into it.


Whichever one you landed on, you don't have to do it alone in your head at 1am. You can talk it through with Maia on your own first, or bring your partner in when you're ready to have the conversation together. Maia won't tell you to stay or go. It helps you say what you mean and hear what comes back.
